findings.title: Wrong lightness in embedded post author link color conversion
findings.body: This conversion changes the light-theme branch from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), even though only the dark-theme branch needed adding. In light themes embedded-post author/reply links become much lighter than before (30% to 70%), reducing contrast and changing the intended hierarchy. The conversion should keep $primary at 30% and use $secondary at 70% for dark themes.

findings.title: Topic map heading color converted with wrong lightness values
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), but the new dark-light-choose uses 50% for both branches. This makes light-theme topic-map headings lighter than before (20% to 50%) and does not use the complementary 80% lightness for $secondary in dark themes. The intended conversion should be scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) / scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%).

findings.title: Group member name color uses 50% instead of original 30%
findings.body: The .group-member-info .name rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The new dark-light-choose uses 50% for both $primary and $secondary, so light-theme group member names are rendered lighter than before and the dark-theme branch is not the complementary $secondary(70%) color. Keep $primary at 30% and use $secondary at 70%.

findings.title: Mobile group member name color loses original lightness
findings.body: This change replaces scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) with dark-light-choose using 50% for both branches. It alters the light-theme color to a lighter gray and does not apply the expected complementary $secondary(70%) value in dark themes. The original $primary(30%) value should be preserved.

findings.title: Custom message length converted with inverted lightness
findings.body: The original color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), but the new light-theme branch uses $primary(30%) and the dark-theme branch uses $secondary(70%). This makes the light-theme text darker than before and misses the complementary dark-theme value. The intended conversion is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) / scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%).
